executive_summary: This collection window (April 13-19, 2027) is the forty-third archived window. FW27-28 women's ready-to-wear and Haute Couture SS27 remain without reachable post-show coverage, unchanged from the prior eleven windows. Two items are logged. First, a genuinely new designer-origin development: Moschino's creative director transition (Loris Messina and Simone Rizzo, the former Sunnei founders, named co-creative directors following Adrian Appiolaza's departure) is well-corroborated across multiple high-reliability editorial outlets and is logged as a new signal, not a status update. Second, 'Glamoratti' (glamoratti-revival, archived 2027-04-05) was checked again: no outlets beyond those already logged in the prior two windows surfaced anything substantively new, so it is not repeated as a top signal this window and is instead noted in limitations as continuing at its prior saturated/medium status with no fresh evidence to report. Per SKILL.md workflow note 10, Wales Bonner/Hermes and the CFDA Fashion Fund/Awards questions were checked briefly and not re-litigated: no coverage beyond what is already archived was found. collection_status is set to 'normal' this window given the genuinely new, independently corroborated Moschino signal, distinguishing it from the prior several 'thin' windows.

top_signals.name: Moschino creative director transition: Messina/Rizzo (ex-Sunnei) named co-creative directors
top_signals.evidence: Moschino announced June 21, 2026 that Loris Messina and Simone Rizzo -- who co-founded and exited Sunnei in 2024 -- are its new co-creative directors, effective immediately, two days after Adrian Appiolaza's departure. Reported independently by WWD, W Magazine, and FashionUnited (among others), all citing a designer statement that the pair intend to carry forward Franco Moschino's 'cultural house' approach; their debut collection is scheduled for Milan Fashion Week in September 2026.
top_signals.index_note: New signal_id (moschino-messina-rizzo-appointment); checked all existing signal_ids across all 42 prior reports before writing, no collision. Distinct from the already-tracked armani-founder-transition and versace-mulier-debut-unconfirmed executive-change signals -- separate house, separate event.
top_signals.human_editor_note: Classified as 'flash' volatility rather than 'emerging' or 'stable': an executive appointment is a discrete, dated event, not a gradually building aesthetic shift, so the volatility label describes how the story broke (a single dense burst of near-simultaneous editorial coverage around the announcement date) rather than a trend gaining momentum over time. Confidence held at 'medium' rather than 'high' because all corroborating sources sit in the same source_sectors bucket (editorial) -- per derive_confidence(), 'high' requires corroboration across at least two distinct sectors, and no designer_origin (Moschino's own site) or institutional confirmation was found in this search pass, only third-party editorial reporting of the designers' quoted statement. Worth watching whether the September 2026 Milan debut produces runway-sector coverage that would change that.
